source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Nominations for County and Rural Councils")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name checked against the page image; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Election of the county council, 1946, the first after the wartime postponement of the 1942 and 1945 elections: nominations received by W. Jenkinson, returning officer, 19 September 1946; contests in Armagh and Lurgan, polled 3 October 1946. The Belfast News-Letter prints no party labels, so none are given for the unopposed members. Hawthorne, Richardson, McCreesh and Mrs. Greeves were new members. Returned unopposed. M. M'Creesh: no party label printed in 1946. At other elections he stood as Anti-Partitionist (Forkhill, Newry No. 2 Rural District, 2 June 1949, printed 'Anti-Partitionist': Newry Telegraph, 21 May 1949, p. 3 ("Newry No. 2 (Co. Armagh) Rural District Council (election nominations)"); Frontier Sentinel, 21 May 1949, p. 3 ("Newry and Kilkeel Rural Councils' Nominations")). The name stands at elections from 1927 to 1964 and may be a father and son.
